column5: If means only when something happens (false, if is not only when) => If tells us what must happen first; also .002 and .007
But joins opposite ideas. => But joins ideas that are different.
A dictionary does not tell us who first said a word. => A dictionary does not usually tell us who first said a word.
Which letter comes after m (o and p also come after m) => comes right after m
hint Between a and o, but cave has second letter a => look at the third letter too; explanation now gives both reasons
Short words take -er (more fun, more real) => Short words like big take -er
consonant + y always changes to i (shy, shyer) => usually; also er-est.807
one vowel and one last consonant doubles (low, new do not) => one short vowel
never put more in front of an -er word (more clever, more eager) => a comparing word like higher
Big has one vowel and one consonant (it has two consonants) => one short vowel and ends in one consonant; hint Short words double (long, fast) => like big
True or false: hottest has two t letters, keyed True, and hottest has three => has a double t in the middle; hint Count the ts => look after the o
Too means also, or very (too hot is not very hot) => also, or more than is needed
A herd is a group of cows => a group of animals, such as cows; also .012
Knight is a man who rode a horse. => A knight was a soldier who rode a horse.
keyed option said the Moon changes shape => seems to change shape, explanation too
Titles tell us what a text is about. => Titles often tell us what a text is about.
prompt asked about children, the picture shows one child => the child, hint too
Describe what the animals are doing, the icons show no action => Say what each animal might be doing
We only add -es after s, sh, ch, x or z (false: tomatoes, potatoes) => Cat ends in t, so it just adds -s; same note in .005
Words ending in s, sh, ch, x, z add -es (stomachs) => Most words; .002 .004 .006 .801 .804
spell babies, hint said It does not end in s => It does not end in ys
Strawberry has two r letters (it has three, and the wrong label strawbery has two) => The berry part has two
ready: covering re leaves ady, note said Dy => Ady
untidy, hint Three letters plus tidy, un has two => Two letters
Un- and dis- mean not, in an item with unpack => often mean not
words that mean not => words with a prefix that means not, explanation too
The first spoken word always starts with a capital letter => The first spoken word starts with a capital letter
These are only the first word. => This is only the first word.
groups Has speech / Has no speech, but Dina said hello does report speech => Has speech marks / No speech marks
spoken words followed by said take a comma (questions and exclamations do not) => spoken words that tell something
rubric asks for speech marks, model had none => one line of speech added, also .012
This comes in the middle. => This usually comes later in the story.
Sighed shows a breath of tiredness. => Sighed shows a long breath, not a loud voice.
Use at least two speech marks. => Use speech marks at least twice.
-ly tells how (friendly, lovely) => often tells how; .005 .017
consonant + y changes before -ly and -ful (shyly) => usually; .006 .012 .805
all words in -le change -le to -ly (solely, palely) => words like gentle and simple, many words
Peaceless is not a word, and it does not tell how. => Peaceless would mean without peace, and it does not tell how.
Use without something is useless. => Something with no use is useless.
When the suffix -ful starts with a consonant, the silent e stays. => The suffix -ful starts with a consonant, so the silent e in hope stays.
Brave means not afraid (brave people can be afraid) => ready to face danger; opposite hint too
Warm, boiling and scorching are hot. Chilly, freezing and icy are cold. => Warm, boiling and scorching go with hot. Chilly, freezing and icy go with cold.
not about movement: sleep is not movement either, two answers => not a doing word, why notes too
hint Think of the lion, no lion anywhere => the saying as brave as a lion
They both mean very sad => They both mean sad
Am needs an -ing word (I am happy) => With visit, am needs -ing
on Sunday, today is Monday: will go and are going fit the coming Sunday => yesterday, on Sunday
Sing and eat change their whole word. => Sing and eat do not add ed.
Present tense verbs tell us what is happening now. => Present tense verbs can tell us what is happening now.
The cover only shows the title. => The cover does not list the topics in the book.
A story is made up. => Many stories are made up.
why on Mina eats beans and Mina likes mornings said only one detail, the text says neither => The text does not say that
